content.text: (ProAir HFA, ProAir RespiClick, Ventolin HFA, Proventil HFA)
: binding at beta-2 receptors causes relaxation of bronchiole smooth muscle/bronchodilation
, used PRN for acute symptoms (quickly reverses bronchospasm)
: nervousness, tremor, tachycardia, palpitations, cough, hyperglycemia, hypokalemia
Direct Acting – mimic NE/EPI by directly binding to adrenoreceptor
New Asthma guidelines (GINA 2019) recommend low-dose budesonide/formoterol 80-4.5mcg inhaler over albuterol (SABA) for preferred as-needed rescue inhaler
: block constricting action of acetylcholine at M3 receptors in bronchial smooth muscle resulting in bronchodilation; also ⇣ mucus secretion
: may be used in combination w/ SABAs during exacerbations
: Myasthenia gravis, narrow-angle glaucoma, urinary retention, BPH, bladder neck obstruction
: dry mouth, blurred vision, thirst, dry eyes
: act directly at parasympathetic postganglionic cholinergic muscarinic receptors & compete reversibly w/ ACh for receptor binding
: Parkinson’s, motion sickness, respiratory disorders, GI disorders, urinary disorders, hyperhidrosis
: dry mouth, URTIs, cough, bitter taste
*Spiriva Respimat 1.25mcg is indicated for asthma and 2.5mcg is for COPD
Cartridge needs to be inserted in Respimat inhalers prior to use
IV ⇢ indicated in patients w/ impending or actual respiratory arrest or intolerant to PO steroids
MOA: anti-inflam via multi actions on several types of leukocytes
Stim gastric acid & pepsin prod -> take w food
Admin: IV for critically ill, PO, rectal
Admin: IV for critically ill, PO, rectal

: cortisol, as well as other steroid hormones, binds to intracellular receptors – the steroid-receptor complex enters the nucleus and acts as a transcription factor to turn on certain genes, causing synthesis of specific proteins which are responsible for its physiological actions
Increases BG, increases protein catabolism from muscle/bone, antagonist of insulin
Inhibits number/activity of cells involved in inflammatory response
Inhibits histamine release from mast cells
Mineralocorticoid effects: salt/water retention, potassium loss
•Replacement therapy: adrenal insufficiency (Addison's disease) and congenital adrenal hyperplasia (defects in enzymes for steroid hormone synthesis)
•Dexamethasone suppression test (DST): diagnosis of Cushing’s syndrome
•Treatment of chronic inflammatory diseases:  RA, ulcerative colitis, asthma, SLE, eye and skin inflammation
•Treatment of allergic reactions: drug, serum, and transfusion reactions
•Immunosuppression: prevention of graft rejection after transplantation
: increased appetite/weight gain, fluid retention, emotional instability, insomnia, indigestion, bitter taste, increased BP/BG

: osteoporosis, GI (ulceration, bleeding), psychiatric (mood, psychosis), cataracts, glaucoma, CV (HTN, edema, hypokalemia), diabetes, hyperlipidemia, Cushingoid syndrome, growth failure, impaired wound healing, adrenal suppression, immunosuppression
